sources: Maestro's first drafts, from the theory core's notes (PLAN.md tasks 2.2 to 2.5)
Drums: the Groove MIDI Dataset's counts (Google LLC, CC BY 4.0), maestro/data/grooves.json (task 3.3)

Trap's entry (task 3.4a, DadCraft's choices Oct 24): ideas in our own words from Wikipedia's "Trap music", "Drill music" and "Roland TR-808" (CC BY-SA 4.0), Ben Duinker's "Good Things Come in Threes: Triplet Flow in Recent Hip-Hop Music" (Popular Music 38/3, 2019) and producers' guides (ideas only); docs/data.md, "Trap, a closer look"

rhythm.why: 16ths with triplet and 32nd turns; sparse kicks.

feel.why: Half-time: hats ride 16ths under a half-time kick and snare.

vocabulary.why: Dark minor: harmonic minor's V, the bII.

leading.why: Dark, wide, sparse pads; little fuss.

progressions.why: Harmony barely moves: one or two chords, a chord every one or two bars; the 808 carries it. A section keeps its loop, and a phrase mostly just goes round rather than closing on V to i.

one chord.why: a single dark chord: the 808 and the melody do the moving

i to VI.why: home and the chord a semitone over its fifth, two bars each: trap's commonest pair

phrygian pair.why: home and the bII a semitone above: phrygian's darkest colour

minor plagal.why: home and its subdominant, a bar each

harmonic minor.why: home and harmonic minor's major V, its leading tone a semitone under home

bright pair.why: for a bright key (melodic trap): home and its relative minor, two bars each

variants.why: Rounds mostly come back as they were.

members.why: Dark strings, an 808, a bell lead (DadCraft, Oct 24: the bell and the strings).

pad.why: slow strings (GM's String Ensemble 2), holding each chord

bass.why: The 808: no pattern of its own, a note on every kick held to the next, mostly roots, some fifths and octave jumps; now and then a slide into the next note (DadCraft, Oct 24: about 1 in 6). A synth bass stands in for the 808.

melody.why: a bell (GM's glockenspiel): a short dark motif, repeated and varied, a beat of it often in triplets over the straight grid (triplet flow)

develop.why: Triplet figures over the 16ths; the motif comes back close.

drums.why: Half-time: hip hop's kick over two bars, the snare fixed on 3, the hats in 16ths turning to triplets or 32nds for a beat, rolls into each phrase, no tom fills.
